liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **They Love Each Other** (1 review): They Love Each Other is a favorite with a very unusual triple encore [32]
- **Beat It On Down The Line** (1 other source): Last time performed, first since November 11, 1970 [3]

## Setlist highlights

- **Dupree's Diamond Blues**: cut on the recording [1]
- **Not Fade Away**: cut on the recording [1]

## The recordings

- **gd1984-06-21.132583.Nak100CP4.Hill.Keo.Flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 26 songs; 163 min [1]
- **gd1984-06-21.145045.nak.blend.ackerman.miller.noel.t-flac1644**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 163 min [8]
- **gd1984-06-21.151253.fm.eaton.miller.flac2496**: FM broadcast; 22 songs; 169 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [9]. Said about its sound: Broadcast mix has cymbals too loud and keys buried [9]
- **gd1984-06-21.nak300.ackerman.andrewf.32640.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 22 songs; 169 min; rated 3.75/5 by 8 [13]. Said about its sound: SBDs and FM feeds are noisy; this audience recording is better [34]
- **gd1984-06-21.sbd.liberated-Boot.devos.352.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 147 min; rated 3.1/5 by 10 [16]. Said about its sound: Recording has a distant big shed sound similar to Alpine or Poplar Creek; A significant portion of Space is missing from this copy [24][30]

## Around the show

- Kingswood was far outside Toronto, requiring travel through farmland [28]
- Crowd started moving and boogieing as the band began playing [31]
- Rick Danko joined the Dead for encores, looking like a kid playing with Jerry [33]
- Attendees stayed at the airport Hilton Hotel after the show [33]
- The Band opened for the Dead; event was a SEVA Benefit [8]
- April first show takes first prize in the 1984 pack [24]
- Performance lacks oomph; only the encore with the Band is recommended [28]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1984-06-21.132583.Nak100CP4.Hill.Keo.Flac2496**: taped by Steve Hill; transferred by Keo; source: Master Audience Recorded By Steve Hill, Transfer By Keo; Nakamichi CM100/CP4 Shotguns > Sony D5, Tapes:Maxell UDXLII 90's; Tapes Labelled:Nakamichi 100 Guns -… [1]
- **gd1984-06-21.145045.nak.blend.ackerman.miller.noel.t-flac1644**: taped by Ray Ackerman; transferred by Edited & Mastered by Joe Noel; source: Ray Ackerman’s Master Audience Cassettes; 2 Nakamichi CM-300's w/ CP-4 shotguns capsules + 1 Nakamichi CM-300 w/ CP-1 cardioid capsule blend mic > Nakamichi… [8]. Also: Edited and mastered by Joe Noel using Audacity and FLAC 24/96 [8]
- **gd1984-06-21.151253.fm.eaton.miller.flac2496**: transferred by Recording, Transfer and Mastering by Rob Eaton Additional Mastering by Charlie Miller  December 24, 2020; source: FM > Cassette Master (Tascam 122) [9]. Also: FM patch source needed pitch correction plus 2.0 percent [9]
- **gd1984-06-21.nak300.ackerman.andrewf.32640.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Ray Ackerman; source: Two Nakamichi CM-300's with CP-4 shotguns capsules, plus one Nakamichi CM-300 with CP-1 cardioid capsule blend mic > Nakamichi MX-100 mixer > passed thru Sony… [13]
- **gd1984-06-21.sbd.liberated-Boot.devos.352.shnf**: transferred by Boudewijn de Vos; source: "liberated" Bootleg CD > EAC > SHN [16]. Also: Recorded directly off the satellite feed at a public radio station [30]
